record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and file listing only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes after activation-space steering with mean-difference directions, a different intervention from the original projection ablation. It therefore tests the effect of direction-based steering on refusal, but does not report the original ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal rates for per-category steering, held-out steering and controls, cross-subset steering, and multi-category steering. It also gives routing-classifier scores and direction cosines; those are not rows because they do not measure refusal outcomes. Reported train/held-out values and held-out evaluation values are kept separate. The repo contains result files, but the code was not read or run.
record.test_reason: A GitHub demo repo, read from the README only. On Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct it removes mean-difference refusal directions at inference time (the reposition update from arXiv:2512.16602, not projection ablation). It reports refusal rates before and after, on train, held-out and never-seen prompts. The setting is new: refusals on politically and religiously sensitive topics, not harmful instructions. So it bears on the removal half of V1 in that setting. It is a tool demo, but it reports the behaviour's rate under the intervention, so it is more than T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The README presents mean-difference reposition steering as removing sensitive-topic refusals on Qwen2.5-1.5B, including on never-seen prompts and over-refused controls, with coherent outputs. It notes religion residual deflections, entangled routing, and that SVD composition is not worse than naive stacking, not better. It also stresses that the keyword judge undercounts deflection refusals, so true steered refusal exceeds 0%.
record.recipe_differences: This is a tool/demo implementing a different cited paper's mean-difference directions and reposition update, with per-category layer and strength selection. It does not use the original all-layer, all-position projection ablation. The README reports no weight edit.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by category and steering configuration: selected layer is L26 for China and L27 for India, US, and religion; held-out forced steering leaves 7% religion refusal, and auto-routing has residual refusal on China and India prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: The india, us and religion category directions have pairwise cosines of 0.82–0.91. One top singular component holds 90% of their stacked energy. Two China subset directions have cosine 0.67 with each other.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal directions built from different sensitive-topic categories share one dominant generic refusal axis plus category residuals.

record.problems: README-only evidence; the sweep and held-out refusal judge is keyword-based, and the README notes it can miss paraphrased deflections. A 20-pair spot-check against a Groq LLM judge showed 90% agreement. No broad capability evaluation is reported; coherence checks do not establish preservation of general capabilities.
record.rows_left_out: No README-reported refusal outcome rows were left out. Router-classifier scores and direction cosine/SVD-energy measurements were not included because they do not report refusal outcomes.

untested.parts: The direction is built from sensitive-topic prompts, not harmful-minus-harmless instructions. No all-layer projection ablation is run. Adding the direction to induce refusal is not tested. General capability preservation is not measured; only coherence and length checks are given.

missing.what: Cross-category entanglement under auto-routing. The China hook fired on only 7/44 China prompts, yet only 2/44 stayed refused. 16 baseline refusals were unblocked by a non-China category hook.
Judge dependence. A 20-pair keyword vs LLM-judge spot-check agreed 90%. The disagreements were steered deflection refusals, so true post-steering refusal is above 0%.
Direction-method dependence. In the sweep, the ridge-regularised rmd direction was mostly negative for every category; plain md worked.
race_gender category not shipped. Baseline refusal was only 17%, and the sweep found no signal.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is README-only, from an unreviewed demo repo. The prompts are sensitive-topic (censorship-style) refusals, not harmful requests, which is why I set the tranche to T3. Layer and alpha were selected per category by a sweep, but the reported numbers are on splits the sweep did not see. I changed r17 and r18 from partial to observed because they are near-complete removal.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original harmful-minus-harmless direction followed by projection out at every layer and position; does not add the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; does not measure broad general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak suppression or adversarial training against ablation is tested.
The category-vector SVD composition is evaluated, but the study does not test whether refusal is generally better described as affine, a cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No separate harmfulness-judgment measure is reported.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer is tested. The China prompt-subset check is within one model.
No comparison of refusal training procedures or training stages is reported.
